name: Diploma of Business
description: This course covers the everyday running of a small organisation: planning work, writing business documents, handling money and leading a small team. Classes are practical, with simulated workplace tasks and short projects set in a workshop room.

name: Diploma of Leadership and Management
description: Built for people who already supervise others or are about to. You practise coaching, giving feedback, planning rosters and resolving conflict, then apply the methods in a workplace project assessed by your supervisor.

name: Diploma of Accounting
description: Students learn to keep ledgers, prepare payroll, reconcile accounts and lodge tax reports using common accounting software. Most of the work is done on case files drawn from small trading businesses.

name: Diploma of Marketing and Communication
description: You plan and run small campaigns from audience research through to a written report on how they went. Practical studios cover copywriting, social media scheduling, basic design briefs and event promotion.

name: Diploma of Project Management
description: This diploma teaches how a project is scoped, scheduled, costed and closed. Learners build plans in standard tools and present them to a panel, then adjust the plan after a staged change request.

name: Diploma of Human Resources Management
description: Covers recruitment, induction, record keeping and the basic rules that apply to employing people in Australia. You work through role plays and sample files, including a mock hiring round and a performance review.

name: Diploma of Logistics
description: A hands-on course about moving goods from supplier to customer. Students plan loads, read freight documents, track inventory in a warehouse system and spend time on a work placement with a distribution site.

name: Diploma of Business Administration
description: Over two years you learn the office systems that keep a business running, from spreadsheets and databases to records and reporting. The second year adds a structured placement and a project improving a real administrative process.

name: Master of Business Administration
description: A general management degree for people with some work behind them. Teaching is by case discussion and group consulting projects, moving from strategy and finance to leading change inside an organisation.

name: Master of Accounting
description: Designed for graduates from outside accounting who want to move into the field. You study financial reporting, auditing and taxation through worked examples, and sit a placement in a practice or finance team.

name: Master of Marketing
description: One year of study into how organisations understand buyers and decide what to offer. Assessment mixes research reports, campaign plans and a final brand strategy presented to a client brief.

name: Master of Human Resource Management
description: This course examines how organisations hire, develop and retain people. You read research on motivation and workplace relations, then apply it in case studies on pay, training and restructuring.

name: Master of Supply Chain Management
description: The course follows a product from raw material to customer, looking at purchasing, production, storage and transport. Students model networks in software, visit distribution sites and complete an industry-linked project in the second year.

name: Diploma of Business Management
description: A pathway diploma that introduces the main functions of a firm: money, people, markets and operations. Small classes and weekly assignments help students settle into university-style study before moving on to a degree.

name: Master of Information Systems Management
description: Looks at how organisations choose, build and govern the technology their work depends on. You analyse business needs, map processes and write the case for new systems, with a team project on a live problem.

name: Master of Business Administration (Global)
description: A management degree that treats the firm as part of a wider market. Teaching is by discussion of cases from several economies, with a consulting placement near the end of the course.

name: Master of Commerce (Accounting)
description: You study how financial information is produced, checked and used in decisions. Lectures are paired with tutorial problem sets, and a placement or research report finishes the second year.

name: Master of Marketing and Advertising
description: This one-year course teaches how messages are researched, written and placed across media. Studio-style units have students build a campaign for a brief, test it with a small audience and revise it.

name: Master of Project Management
description: Focused on planning and steering projects with budgets, deadlines and many parties involved. Units use real project documents, and each student leads a team through a simulated project from approval to handover.

name: Master of Logistics and Supply Chain Management
description: Examines transport, warehousing and purchasing as one connected system. You build route and stock models, study case reports and write a research paper on a supply problem of your choice.

name: Diploma of Commerce
description: An introductory year across accounting, economics, marketing and management. Students practise essay writing, basic data handling and presentation skills while sampling each area before they commit to a major.

name: Master of Business Information Systems
description: Combines business analysis with the technology used to support it. You model processes, design databases and manage a software-based change project, ending with a placement that applies these skills.

name: Master of Business Administration (Innovation)
description: A management course where each unit ends in a studio-style project. You work on problems posed by organisations, from pricing to service redesign, and learn to test ideas before committing resources.

name: Master of Professional Accounting
description: Prepares graduates from other disciplines for accounting work. You learn reporting, audit and tax methods from case files, and spend a semester inside a firm or finance department.

name: Master of Marketing
description: Explores how markets are studied and how offers are shaped to fit them. Students analyse consumer data, write marketing plans and defend them in a panel review at the end of the year.

name: Master of Human Resource Management
description: The course teaches how to design jobs, hire fairly and manage change. It leans on workplace case studies, interview practice and a placement in an HR team during the second year.

name: Master of Supply Chain and Operations
description: Concentrates on how goods and services are made and delivered at scale. You use spreadsheets and simulation tools to plan capacity, manage stock and compare supplier options.

name: Master of Actuarial Studies
description: You learn to measure and price financial risk using probability, statistics and insurance mathematics. Units combine proofs with computer-based modelling, and a placement in a risk team closes the degree.

name: Master of Financial Technology
description: A one-year course on the software behind payments, lending and trading. You write small programs, study how digital financial products are regulated and build a working prototype with a team.

name: Master of Design and Business Strategy
description: Teaches how designers and managers work together to shape services and products. You use interviews, journey maps and prototypes to inform business decisions, and develop a project with an outside organisation.

name: Master of Business Administration
description: A degree for working professionals who want broader management skills. Lectures are short and discussion-led, and the final year centres on a project solving a problem in an organisation of your choice.

name: Master of Accounting
description: Covers financial reporting, auditing and tax in a sequence that assumes no prior accounting study. Tutorials use company reports and sample audit files for practice.

name: Master of Marketing
description: Students investigate how products are positioned, priced and promoted, using real data sets and client briefs. A short industry placement lets you apply the planning methods to a working marketing team.

name: Master of Entrepreneurship and Innovation
description: Looks at how new ventures start and grow. You test an idea with customers, build a simple financial model and pitch to a small panel, learning from what does not work.

name: Diploma of Business
description: A pathway year for students new to university. Subjects in accounting, management and marketing are taught in small groups with extra help for writing and numbers.

name: Master of Business Analytics
description: Teaches how to turn business data into decisions. You work in a statistics language and visualisation tools, build models for sales and customer questions, and spend a semester on an analytics placement.

name: Master of Financial Technology and Innovation
description: This course joins finance and software, from how markets and banks work to how digital platforms are built. Students code small trading and lending tools and test them on historical data.

name: Master of Strategic Design Management
description: Introduces the planning side of design work: how to set a brief, run a team of creatives and link design choices to what an organisation is trying to achieve. Assessment is through reports, studio reviews and one client-style pitch.

name: Master of Business Administration
description: A management degree with a focus on organisations in regional and island settings. You study strategy, money and people through cases and finish with a consulting project with a local organisation.

name: Master of Professional Accounting
description: Designed for graduates from other fields. Over two years you learn to prepare and check financial statements, apply tax law and understand how audits are carried out.

name: Master of Marketing
description: This course teaches how to find and understand customers and shape messages for them. Projects often use tourism, food and small producers as settings, and students write a plan for a real business.

name: Master of Supply Chain and Logistics
description: You study how goods travel by sea, road and air, with a focus on isolated markets and cold-chain products. Fieldwork at ports and packing sheds is part of the course, alongside planning exercises.

name: Diploma of Business Management
description: A first-year pathway into management study. Students learn the basics of accounting, marketing and leading a team, and complete a small group project for a local organisation.

name: Master of Human Resource Management
description: Concentrates on the practical side of managing people: hiring, training, handling disputes and keeping records. Students interview managers, work through role plays and write a report on a workplace problem.

name: Master of Actuarial Science and Finance
description: Teaches the mathematics of insurance, pensions and investment. The first year is heavy on probability and statistics, and the second applies them to pricing and reserving problems on spreadsheets and code.

name: Diploma of Business Analysis
description: Introduces how analysts gather requirements, describe processes and test whether a system does what staff need. You practise in small teams with sample systems used in the workplace.

name: Master of Business Administration
description: A management degree built around industry projects. You study strategy, finance and leadership with practising managers, and carry out a consulting assignment for an organisation in the second year.

name: Master of Accounting and Finance
description: Combines the preparation of financial reports with the study of how companies raise and invest money. You work through ledgers, valuation exercises and an end-of-course placement.

name: Master of Marketing
description: Teaches how to learn from customers and design marketing that responds to them. Assessments include a research study, a communication plan and a reflective journal on how methods were used.

name: Master of Supply Chain Management
description: Looks at planning, buying and moving goods through networks of firms. Students use planning software, study disruption cases and write a recommendation on a supply problem.

name: Diploma of Business Studies
description: This pathway diploma introduces the main parts of business through short units and regular feedback. It suits people returning to study who want support with writing, reading and number work.

name: Master of Actuarial Practice
description: A professional course in valuing risk for insurers and pension funds. You apply statistical models to claims data, learn the standards actuaries work to, and complete a placement in a risk or pricing team.

name: Master of Financial Technology
description: Students study how digital tools change banking, payments and investing. You build small applications, review how rules apply to them and present a prototype and a risk assessment at the end.

name: Master of Design Innovation and Strategy
description: You learn to plan and lead design-led projects, working from user research through to a strategy for change. Teamwork with outside organisations runs through the second year.

name: Master of Business Administration
description: A general management course taught through cases, group work and live assignments. Students move from the core areas of business to a major project that tests their ability to lead change.

name: Master of Professional Accounting
description: You learn financial reporting, auditing and tax from the ground up and apply them to company reports. A placement or applied project follows the coursework.

name: Master of Marketing
description: This course shows how research on buyers guides decisions about products, prices and messages. You analyse data, write plans and critique real campaigns in seminars.

name: Master of Human Resource Management
description: Students examine how people are recruited, developed and led. Seminars use case studies on workforce change, fairness at work and the design of reward systems.

name: Master of Supply Chain Management
description: The course connects procurement, production and delivery, with an emphasis on data and planning tools. A placement in the second year gives students a chance to apply network models to a real supply problem.

name: Master of Actuarial Science
description: A mathematically demanding course on pricing, reserving and managing financial risk. Students learn stochastic and statistical methods and implement them in code before a placement in an insurer or consultancy.

name: Master of Financial Technology
description: Combines programming, data and finance in a single year. You build tools for payments, credit scoring and trading, and study the rules that apply to financial firms.

name: Master of Business Analytics
description: You learn to collect, clean and model business data and then explain the results to managers. Teaching mixes statistics, programming and case-based communication tasks.

name: Master of Business Administration
description: A management degree you can study with mostly online teaching alongside campus intensives. The course covers strategy, people and finance, and ends with a project inside a workplace.

name: Master of Professional Accounting
description: Taught in plain steps for students new to accounting. You prepare financial statements, learn about tax and study how audits are planned and reported.

name: Master of Marketing
description: This one-year course teaches planning for products, services and brands. Students work with a regional organisation to draft and test a marketing plan, and meet staff for feedback.

name: Master of Supply Chain and Logistics
description: Teaches the planning of storage, transport and buying across manufacturing and retail. Students use inventory and routing tools and compare cost with service in case-based tasks.

name: Master of Human Resource Management
description: Develops skills in hiring, training and handling employment matters. Students read research, practise structured interviews and write workplace policy documents.

name: Diploma of Business
description: A pathway year with a broad look at accounting, management and marketing. Classes are small and include structured help with study skills before entry into a degree.

name: Master of Financial Technology
description: You learn the technology and rules behind modern finance, from software design to data security and consumer protection. A placement with a finance or software team follows two semesters of project work.

name: Master of Information Systems and Business Analysis
description: Looks at how organisations plan, buy and run their information systems. Students practise writing requirements, mapping processes and evaluating what a new system will change.

name: Graduate Diploma of Actuarial Studies
description: A one-year diploma in the core mathematics behind insurance and superannuation. You work through probability, statistics and financial maths, mainly by problem sets and computer exercises.

name: Diploma of Design Thinking for Business
description: Shows how to approach business problems like a designer: talk to users, sketch options, test them cheaply and refine. Most of the course is workshop-based, with a final project on a problem set by a local organisation.

name: Diploma of Financial Technology
description: An introduction to how digital tools are used in payments, lending and investing. Students learn basic coding and spreadsheet modelling and look at how rules shape what a financial product can do.

name: Master of Design Leadership
description: A one-year course on leading creative teams and linking design to a firm's aims. You study how decisions are made in design practices and work on a brief with a mentor.

name: Master of Actuarial Studies
description: Provides training in the models actuaries use to value risk. Study moves from probability and statistics to insurance products, and students use spreadsheets and code throughout.

name: Diploma of Business Analytics
description: You learn to handle data in spreadsheets and a simple programming language, draw charts and write findings in plain language. Projects use sales, customer and finance data sets.

name: Diploma of Business Analytics
description: Learners clean, summarise and chart business data using spreadsheets and a reporting tool. The work is practical and based on short workplace scenarios, ending in a one-page briefing to a manager.

name: Diploma of Financial Services
description: A practical course for people who want to work in banks, brokers or advice firms. You learn how to explain products, record client details correctly and follow the rules that apply to selling them, with a short work placement.

name: Diploma of Digital Marketing
description: Learners plan and run online campaigns through search, email and social platforms. Weekly studio tasks involve writing content, reading simple reports and adjusting a campaign.
